The firm combines direct and indirect tax, CFO-level financial advice, strategy, transactions and cross-border work, led by its partners rather than delegated.

Managing Partner

An entrepreneur himself, Varun co-founded Health-E, a health-tech platform, in 2020. This experience shaped his understanding of the challenges involved in building and scaling businesses, from strategy and finance to execution.

His perspectives on entrepreneurship, economics, taxation, corporate laws and finance have been featured at platforms including the i5 Summit at IIM Indore, Anveeksha at AIMIT, and national conferences organised by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI).

Over the course of his professional journey, Varun has worked with businesses across technology, e-commerce, real estate, construction, consumer goods and retail, as well as listed companies. His engagements have included strategic expansion, cross border transaction advisory, capital raising and financial structuring, due diligence, providing exposure to businesses at different stages of growth and across diverse sectors.

At Varish Partners, Varun leads client relationships and contributes to business strategy, finance and the firm’s overall management. He works closely with founders, promoters and management teams on strategic decisions, growth initiatives, capital requirements and complex financial matters.

# Our Story
Source: https://www.varishpartners.com/our-story/

Varish Partners was built on a simple observation: most businesses don't fail their financial and tax obligations out of neglect — they fail them because good advice arrives too late, or too generic to act on. Founded by Varun Shenoy and Vishwanath Prabhu, professionals with over two decades of combined experience across tax, compliance, and corporate advisory, the firm set out to close that gap: advice that arrives before a decision is made, not after it's already cost something.

What started as tax and compliance support for individuals and small businesses grew, as our clients grew, into a full consultancy practice — covering business registration, GST, financial planning, fractional CFO support, and transaction advisory. The common thread has stayed the same throughout: we work alongside clients through the year, not just at deadlines, and we measure our work by whether it actually moved the client's business forward.

### A Story That Defines How We Work

One engagement in particular captures what that looks like in practice. A client came to us for their overseas expansion — advice on the right investment strategy, and a way through the complexity of cross-border taxation and transfer pricing. The timelines were tight, so the team built a comprehensive proposal upfront, laying out exactly where we'd focus and why, then worked through the engagement with the same discipline: a concise final report, risks clearly categorised, delivered on schedule.

The result was concrete — the client moved into a new international market with an anticipated 20% increase in investment potential, and the risk mitigation work built into our advice is expected to cut their compliance costs by roughly 25%. It's one of many client stories, but it's a fair example of the standard we hold ourselves to: proactive planning, clear deliverables, and outcomes clients can actually measure.

### Where we are today

Today, Varish Partners supports individuals, startups, and established businesses across tax consultancy, GST compliance, financial planning, and business advisory — the same client-first approach the firm was founded on, applied at a larger scale. Read more about our mission, values, and leadership, or get in touch to start a conversation.

# Tax Advisory & Compliance
Source: https://www.varishpartners.com/tax-consultancy-compliances/

Helping businesses manage tax efficiently, compliantly and strategically.

Tax touches almost every decision a business makes, from how it is structured to how it prices, pays and grows. We advise on direct and indirect tax together, so the position you take in one never creates a problem in the other, and we stay with you through filings, reviews and disputes.

What all includes

## Direct & Indirect Tax Advisory

Income tax and GST are usually handled by different people, which is where gaps and double costs appear. We look at both together, advise on the tax impact of day-to-day business decisions, and give you clear positions you can rely on when filing and when questioned.

## Corporate & International Tax

Companies face questions on residence, permanent establishment, foreign income and cross-border payments as soon as they deal overseas. We advise on corporate tax positions at home and on how international activity is taxed, so profits are not taxed twice and reporting stays consistent.

## Tax Planning & Structuring

The right structure, set up early, saves far more than any year-end adjustment. We review how your business, its entities and its owners are organised and recommend arrangements that are efficient, commercially sensible and able to stand up to scrutiny.

## Transaction Tax Advisory

Acquisitions, share sales, mergers and restructurings each carry tax consequences that can change the value of the deal. We model those consequences before terms are fixed and advise on structures that protect value for buyers, sellers and promoters.

## GST Advisory & Compliance

We handle GST registrations, monthly and annual returns, reconciliations and input tax credit reviews, and advise on classification, place of supply and e-invoicing questions. The aim is simple: no credit lost to avoidable errors and no surprises when the department asks questions.

## TDS & Withholding Tax Advisory

Getting withholding wrong leads to interest, disallowed expenses and unhappy vendors and employees. We advise on the correct rates and sections for domestic and foreign payments, manage quarterly returns and certificates, and help with lower-deduction applications where they apply.

## Tax Reviews & Health Checks

A periodic review finds exposures while they are still cheap to fix. We go through your income tax, GST and TDS positions, filings and records, and give you a clear list of gaps, their likely cost and the steps to close them before an audit or notice does it for you.

## Transfer Pricing Advisory

Transactions between related entities must be priced as if they were between strangers. We help set and document arm’s length pricing for goods, services, royalties and funding, prepare the required reports, and support you when those prices are examined.

## Tax Due Diligence

Before you invest in or buy a business, you need to know what tax history comes with it. We review past filings, open assessments and risky positions, quantify the exposure, and suggest how it should be handled in the price, warranties or indemnities.

## Tax Litigation & Representation

When a notice, assessment or demand arrives, the quality of the first response often decides the outcome. We draft replies, represent you before tax authorities and appellate forums, and manage disputes with a practical eye on both the merits and the cost of fighting.

Explore services
Schedule a call

Whether you need a single position reviewed or a long-term tax partner, we bring technical depth and practical judgment to every engagement. Contact us to discuss your tax position.

# CFO & Financial Advisory
Source: https://www.varishpartners.com/fractional-cfo-services/

Financial clarity and decision support for growing businesses.

Growing businesses need senior financial thinking long before they can justify a full-time CFO. We give founders and management teams clear numbers, honest analysis and a steady hand on cash, planning and reporting, so decisions are made on facts rather than instinct.

What all includes

## Fractional CFO Services

You get an experienced CFO for the days and hours your business actually needs. We lead the finance function, work alongside your team and advisers, and bring the discipline and perspective of a senior finance leader without the cost of a full-time hire.

## Board & Investor Reporting

Boards and investors want the same things: accurate numbers, a clear story and no surprises. We prepare board packs and investor updates that explain performance, flag risks early and show how the business is tracking against its plan.

## Business Performance Reviews

We step back and look at how the business is really doing across products, customers, locations and teams. The review shows where money is made and lost, how you compare with peers, and which few changes would make the biggest difference.

## Financial Planning & Analysis

Good planning turns strategy into numbers you can manage against. We build the planning cycle, analyse actual results against plan every month, and explain the variances in plain language so management knows what to do next.

## Budgeting & Forecasting

We prepare annual budgets that reflect how the business actually runs, and rolling forecasts that update as conditions change. You see where the year is heading early enough to act, not after the quarter has closed.

## Financial Modelling

A well-built model lets you test decisions before you commit to them. We build clear, auditable models for budgets, new projects, pricing, fundraising and expansion, with scenarios that show what happens when assumptions change.

## Cash Flow & Working Capital

Profitable businesses still fail when cash runs short. We forecast cash week by week, tighten collections, payables and inventory, and free up working capital so growth is funded from within wherever possible.

## Management Reporting & MIS

We design monthly MIS that management actually reads: the handful of numbers that matter, reported on time and in a consistent format. Dashboards and commentary make it easy to spot trends and act on them.

## Profitability & Cost Optimisation

We analyse margins by product, customer and channel to show which parts of the business earn their keep. Then we look at costs line by line and help you cut waste without damaging the things customers value.

## Financial Controls & Process Improvement

Weak processes lead to errors, delays and fraud. We review how money moves through the business, from purchase to payment and from sale to collection, and put in practical controls and cleaner processes that scale as you grow.

Explore services
Schedule a call

Whether you need a part-time CFO, a forecast you can trust or a clearer monthly picture, we will fit the support to the stage your business is at. Contact us to talk it through.

# Strategy & Growth Advisory
Source: https://www.varishpartners.com/strategic-consulting-impact/

Turning business ambitions into executable growth strategies.

Ambition is only useful when it becomes a plan people can act on. We help promoters and leadership teams decide where to compete, how to grow and how to fund that growth, including the government schemes and incentives that many businesses never claim.

What all includes

## Business & Corporate Strategy

We work with leadership to set a clear direction: which markets to play in, which businesses to grow or exit, and how resources should be allocated between them. The result is a strategy that is specific enough to guide everyday decisions.

## Business Model Design & Optimisation

How you make money matters as much as what you sell. We examine your revenue streams, cost structure and delivery model, and redesign them where needed so the business earns more from the same effort.

## Market & Competitive Analysis

We size your market, map the competitors and study what customers actually choose and why. This gives you a fact-based view of where the opportunities are and where you are exposed.

## Business Restructuring

When a business has outgrown its shape or is under pressure, restructuring can restore focus and viability. We plan and support changes to operations, entities, costs and finances, keeping stakeholders informed at every stage.

## Performance Improvement

We identify the few operational and financial levers that most affect results, set targets for them and track progress with management. The focus is on measurable improvement within months, not reports that sit on a shelf.

## Promoter & Management Advisory

Promoters carry decisions that no one else in the business can make for them. We act as a trusted sounding board on growth, succession, governance and personal wealth questions that sit alongside the business.

## Growth Strategy

We lay out the realistic paths to growth, whether new customers, new products, new geographies or acquisitions, and compare them on return, risk and what they demand from the organisation. You leave with a prioritised plan, not a wish list.

## Market Entry & Expansion Strategy

Entering a new city, state or country takes more than a good product. We assess demand, regulation, tax and competition in the target market and recommend the entry route, structure and timing most likely to succeed.

## Go-to-Market Strategy

We help you decide who to sell to first, through which channels, at what price and with what message. A clear go-to-market plan shortens the time from launch to steady revenue.

## Pricing & Revenue Strategy

Pricing is often the fastest route to better margins. We analyse your costs, customers and competitors and recommend pricing and discount structures that grow revenue without losing the customers who matter.

## Funding Requirement Assessment

Before raising money, you need to know how much, when and for what. We work out the real funding need from your plans and cash forecasts, so you raise enough to reach the next milestone without giving away more than necessary.

## Capital Structure Advisory

The mix of equity, debt and internal funds shapes your cost of capital, your control and your flexibility. We recommend a capital structure that suits your stage, cash flows and appetite for risk.

## Debt vs Equity Funding Strategy

Debt is cheaper but must be repaid; equity is patient but dilutes ownership. We compare the options available to you, including bank finance, NBFCs, venture debt and equity investors, and help you choose the right combination.

## Fundraising Readiness

Lenders and investors decide quickly, so your numbers, documents and story need to be ready before the first meeting. We prepare the financial model, information pack and data room, and help you answer the questions they will ask.

## Grant & Incentive Identification

Central and state governments offer grants, subsidies, tax benefits and concessional finance that many businesses never hear about. We review your business, sector and plans to identify the incentives you may be entitled to.

## Central & State Scheme Mapping

Schemes differ widely by state, sector and project size. We map the central and state schemes relevant to your investment, including industrial policies and production-linked incentives, so you can compare locations and plans on their full economics.

## Subsidy & Incentive Optimisation

The way a project is planned, located and phased can change how much support it qualifies for. We help you shape investments to maximise eligible benefits while keeping the commercial logic intact.

## Application & Documentation Support

Incentive applications are detailed and unforgiving of gaps. We prepare and file the applications, project reports and supporting documents, and follow up with the departments concerned until approval.

## Incentive Eligibility & Structuring

Eligibility often depends on the entity, its ownership, the investment category and the timing of spend. We structure your project and entity so it meets the conditions from the outset rather than discovering a mismatch later.

## Post-Sanction Compliance & Claim Support

Approval is only the start; benefits are paid out when conditions are met and claims are filed correctly. We track your obligations, prepare periodic claims and certifications, and help ensure the money you were promised actually arrives.

Explore services
Schedule a call

Whether you are planning your next phase of growth or looking for the funding and incentives to pay for it, we will help you build a plan you can execute. Contact us to start the conversation.

# Transaction & Corporate Advisory
Source: https://www.varishpartners.com/business-advisory-services/

Advising businesses through critical transactions and strategic events.

Acquisitions, sales, investments and restructurings are the moments that shape a business for years. We advise from the first idea to completion, bringing financial, tax and commercial judgment together so you negotiate from knowledge and close on terms that hold up.

What all includes

## M&A Advisory

We support buyers and sellers through the full deal process: identifying and approaching counterparties, evaluating the business, negotiating terms and managing the path to completion, so decisions are made with a clear view of value and risk.

## Acquisitions & Divestitures

Whether you are buying a business to grow or selling a part that no longer fits, we help you prepare, value, negotiate and complete the transaction, and plan the integration or separation that follows.

## Deal Structuring

The same price can be worth very different amounts depending on how a deal is structured. We advise on share versus asset deals, payment terms, earn-outs and consideration so the structure works commercially, legally and for tax.

## Joint Venture Advisory

A joint venture succeeds when the partners agree clearly on contributions, control and exit from the start. We help structure the venture, model its economics and set out the terms that keep the partnership workable.

## Strategic Investments

When you invest in another business, whether a minority stake or a strategic partnership, we assess the target, the fit with your own business and the terms on offer, so the investment supports your strategy rather than distracting from it.

## Financial & Tax Due Diligence

We examine the quality of earnings, working capital, debt and tax history of the business you are dealing with. Our findings feed directly into price, deal terms and protections, so there are fewer surprises after closing.

## Valuation & Financial Modelling

We value businesses and shares using methods that suit the purpose, whether a transaction, fundraising, regulatory filing or internal decision, and build models that show how value moves with each key assumption.

## Transaction Tax Advisory

Every transaction has tax consequences for both sides. We identify them early, compare alternative structures and advise on the approach that protects value while staying on solid technical ground.

## Corporate Restructuring

Group structures built up over years often become complex and inefficient. We advise on mergers, demergers, consolidations and simplifications that reduce cost and risk and make the group easier to manage and invest in.

## Shareholder & Promoter Advisory

We advise promoters and shareholders on ownership, shareholder agreements, family arrangements and the terms of new investment, helping protect their interests while keeping the business able to raise capital and grow.

## Succession & Business Transfer

Passing a business to the next generation, to management or to a buyer takes years of planning to do well. We help promoters plan the timing, structure and tax impact of the transfer so the business and the family are both protected.

Explore services
Schedule a call

Whether you are buying, selling, investing or reorganising, we will help you see the full picture before you commit. Contact us to discuss your transaction.

# Cross-Border & International Advisory
Source: https://www.varishpartners.com/cross-border-international-advisory/

Helping businesses navigate international expansion, investments and transactions.

Going international adds new layers of tax, foreign exchange rules and structuring choices. We advise Indian businesses expanding overseas and foreign businesses entering India, bringing international tax, FEMA and transaction experience together in one team.

What all includes

## Inbound Investment Advisory

Foreign investors coming into India need to know which sectors are open, which approval routes apply and how their investment will be taxed. We advise on the entry route, pricing and reporting requirements, and on how returns can be taken out efficiently.

## Outbound Investment Advisory

Indian businesses investing abroad must follow the overseas investment rules and plan for tax in both countries. We advise on the structure, funding and reporting of overseas investments so they stay compliant and tax-efficient.

## India Entry Strategy for Foreign Businesses

We help foreign companies choose how to enter India, whether through a subsidiary, branch, liaison office or partnership, and support them through setup, registrations and the first years of operation.

## International Expansion Planning

Before you expand into a new country, we help you compare markets on demand, regulation, tax and cost of operation, and plan a phased entry that limits risk while you learn the market.

## Overseas Subsidiary & Entity Structuring

The jurisdiction and form of your overseas entities affect tax, control and future flexibility. We design group structures that support your operations and funding plans and comply with the rules in every country involved.

## Cross-Border Transaction Advisory

Transactions that cross borders involve two tax systems, foreign exchange rules and often different accounting standards. We coordinate these moving parts so the deal is structured, priced and completed correctly on both sides.

## Cross-Border M&A Advisory

We advise on acquisitions and sales involving foreign buyers, sellers or targets, covering valuation, diligence, deal structure and the regulatory approvals and filings needed to close.

## Structuring of Intercompany Transactions

Services, royalties, loans and goods moving between group companies must be structured and priced carefully. We design intercompany arrangements and agreements that reflect real activity and hold up under tax review.

## Repatriation & Remittance Structuring

Getting profits and capital back from an investment should be planned from day one. We advise on the most efficient routes, whether dividends, interest, royalties, fees or buy-backs, and the tax and regulatory steps each one requires.

## Cross-Border Payment & Withholding Advisory

Payments to non-residents raise questions of withholding tax, treaty rates and remittance certification. We advise on the correct treatment before money leaves the country, so neither you nor the recipient faces demands later.

## International Tax Structuring

We design cross-border structures that are tax-efficient and have real commercial substance, taking into account treaties, anti-avoidance rules and global minimum tax developments that increasingly limit aggressive planning.

## Transfer Pricing

We help multinational groups set arm’s length prices for intercompany transactions, prepare benchmarking studies and documentation, and support audits and disputes in India and abroad.

## Double Taxation & Treaty Advisory

Tax treaties can reduce or remove double tax, but only if their conditions are met and properly documented. We advise on treaty eligibility, residency certificates and foreign tax credits so income is not taxed twice.

## FEMA & Regulatory Advisory

Foreign exchange rules govern how money and investments move in and out of India. We advise on FEMA and RBI requirements, handle the required filings, and help resolve delays or defaults through compounding where needed.

Explore services
Schedule a call

Whether you are taking your business abroad or bringing your business to India, we will help you do it with the right structure from the start. Contact us to discuss your plans.

# Startup & Venture Advisory
Source: https://www.varishpartners.com/start-up-advisory-and-consultancy-services/

From incorporation to institutional capital and scale.

Founders have to get a lot right early, often with little time and less money. We help startups set up properly, raise capital on sensible terms and build the finance function investors expect, so the business is ready for each stage before it arrives.

What all includes

## Startup Structuring

The entity you choose and how ownership is set up on day one affect fundraising, taxes and exits years later. We help founders choose the right structure, including where international founders or investors are involved, and set it up cleanly.

## Founder & Promoter Advisory

We act as a sounding board for founders on equity splits, vesting, founder agreements, personal tax and the financial side of big decisions, so the relationships at the top stay clear as the company grows.

## Business Planning

We turn your idea into a plan with clear milestones, costs and revenue assumptions. A realistic plan keeps the team aligned and gives investors confidence that you understand your own business.

## Startup Tax Advisory

Startups face specific tax questions around share issues, investor funding, ESOPs and eligible tax holidays. We advise on these early so tax does not become an obstacle during a funding round or due diligence.

## Government Startup Schemes & Incentives

Recognition under the Startup India programme and various state policies can bring tax benefits, grants and easier compliance. We check your eligibility, handle the applications and help you use the benefits available.

## Fundraising Strategy

We help you decide how much to raise, when, from whom and on what instrument, whether equity, convertible notes or venture debt, so each round moves the company forward without unnecessary dilution.

## Investor Readiness

We get your numbers, documents and pitch ready before you meet investors: clean financials, a credible model and a data room that answers questions before they are asked.

## Financial Modelling

We build startup models that investors can follow, linking growth drivers, unit economics, hiring and burn to show how the business reaches its milestones and what happens if assumptions slip.

## Cap Table Structuring

A cap table that is messy or poorly planned can scare off investors. We keep your cap table accurate, model dilution across future rounds and advise on investor rights and share classes.

## ESOP Advisory

Stock options help startups attract and keep good people. We design ESOP schemes, advise on the size of the pool, vesting and valuation, and explain the tax treatment clearly to the company and employees.

## Due Diligence Readiness

We review your records, filings and contracts the way an investor would and fix the gaps before diligence begins, so the round is not delayed or repriced over issues you could have solved in advance.

## Virtual CFO / CFO Support

As you scale, you need senior finance support long before you can hire a full-time CFO. We run your finance function part-time, covering reporting, cash, compliance and investor relations.

## Investor Reporting

Regular, honest investor updates build trust for the next round. We prepare monthly and quarterly reports and board materials that show performance, cash position and progress against plan.

## Exit & Liquidity Planning

Whether the goal is an acquisition, a secondary sale or a public listing, we help founders and investors plan the exit, understand its tax impact and prepare the company to achieve the best value.

Explore services
Schedule a call

Whether you are about to incorporate or preparing for your next round, we will help you build the financial foundations investors look for. Contact us to talk to our team.

# Risk & Due Diligence
Source: https://www.varishpartners.com/risk-due-diligence/

Independent insight into financial, tax and business risks.

Good decisions depend on knowing what could go wrong. We give investors, buyers, lenders and management an independent view of the financial, tax and business risks in front of them, clearly explained and quantified wherever possible.

What all includes

## Financial Due Diligence

We test the numbers behind a business: the quality and sustainability of earnings, working capital, debt and off-balance-sheet items. You learn what you are really paying for and where the price or terms should change.

## Tax Due Diligence

We review past income tax, TDS and related filings, open assessments and aggressive positions, and estimate the potential exposure, so it can be addressed through price, indemnities or pre-closing fixes.

## GST Due Diligence

GST exposures can build up quietly through wrong classifications, credit claims or missed reconciliations. We examine returns, credits and notices to identify liabilities before they become yours.

## Business & Commercial Due Diligence

We look at the market, customers, competitors and business model to test whether the growth story holds up. This helps you judge whether the plan you are backing is realistic.

## Pre-Investment Due Diligence

Before you invest in a company, whether a startup or an established business, we give you a focused review of its finances, compliance and key risks, scaled to the size of the investment and the time available.

## Transaction Due Diligence

For acquisitions, mergers and sales, we coordinate financial, tax and commercial diligence into one clear report, highlighting the issues that affect value and the protections you should seek in the agreement.

## Risk Assessment

We help management identify and rank the risks facing the business, from financial and tax to operational and regulatory, and agree practical actions and owners for the ones that matter most.

## Internal Control Reviews

We test whether your internal controls work in practice, not just on paper, and recommend improvements that reduce errors and fraud without slowing the business down.

Explore services
Schedule a call

Whether you are about to invest, buy, lend or simply want to know where your own business is exposed, we will give you an independent view you can act on. Contact us to discuss your requirements.

# Business Setup, Compliance & Governance
Source: https://www.varishpartners.com/business-registration-services/

Building the financial and regulatory foundation for businesses.

A business built on the right structure and clean compliance is easier to run, fund and sell. We help you set up correctly, keep your books and filings in order every month, and put in the controls and governance that growing businesses need.

What all includes

## Business Incorporation & Structuring

We help you choose between a private company, LLP, partnership or other form, and handle incorporation from name approval to the registrations needed to start trading.

## Entity & Ownership Structuring

How ownership is split between founders, family members, holding companies and investors affects control, tax and future deals. We design ownership structures that are simple today and flexible for tomorrow.

## GST Registration & Compliance

We handle GST registration in the right states and categories, file returns on time, reconcile input tax credit every month and respond to routine departmental queries.

## Accounting & Bookkeeping

We keep your books accurate and up to date, close the accounts every month and prepare financial statements you can rely on for decisions, lenders, investors and tax filings.

## Payroll & TDS

We run monthly payroll, compute tax deductions, manage provident fund and other statutory contributions, and file TDS returns and certificates on time, so employees are paid correctly and the business stays compliant.

## ROC & Corporate Compliance

We manage annual filings with the Registrar of Companies, board and shareholder meetings, statutory registers and event-based filings, so your company stays in good standing and avoids penalties.

## Regulatory Compliance

Beyond tax and company law, businesses must keep up with labour, shops and establishments, import-export and sector-specific rules. We track these obligations and handle the registrations and filings on your behalf.

## Compliance Health Checks

We review your tax, corporate and regulatory compliance in one exercise, identify gaps and penalties at risk, and give you a clear plan to put things right before an audit, fundraise or sale.

## Internal Controls

We put in place the approvals, checks and segregation of duties that protect the business from errors and fraud, sized to your team so controls help rather than slow down daily work.

## SOP & Process Development

Written procedures make work consistent and easier to delegate. We document your finance and compliance processes as clear standard operating procedures that new team members can follow from day one.

## Corporate Governance Advisory

Good governance builds trust with investors, lenders and partners. We advise boards and promoters on board composition, policies, related party transactions and reporting that match the size and ambitions of the business.

# Spotlight: Structuring Around a Regulatory Deadlock in an Industrial Land Acquisition
Source: https://www.varishpartners.com/regulatory-deadlock-industrial-land-acquisition/

22 September 2026 · 5 min read

**Sector:** Strategy & Transaction Advisory. **Engagement type:** Greenfield expansion, industrial land acquisition strategy.

## The Situation

A client planning a strategic greenfield expansion identified a promising industrial site, but the land came with a structural complication. The plot was held by three individual allottees under a 10-year lease-cum-sale agreement with the state’s industrial land development authority, a common allotment structure in Karnataka’s industrial corridors. The district in question is a dense industrial belt, home to multiple designated industrial areas and hundreds of allotted units, making land scarce and highly regulated.

The Client needed operational control of the site immediately, with a clear path to full ownership. The authority’s allotment framework, however, was built to prevent exactly that kind of fast-tracked change of hands.

## The Core Challenge

Lease-cum-sale allotments of this kind exist to ensure land goes to genuine industrial users, not intermediaries. Two features of the framework made a straightforward acquisition impossible:

**The 51% rule.** Until an Absolute Sale Deed is executed, the original allottees are required to retain at least 51% interest in the entity holding the lease.

**Resumption risk.** Any structure that looks like an indirect transfer of the land, or that quietly hands economic and operational control to a third party before the sale deed is executed, exposes the allotment to resumption by the authority, without compensation.

With nine of the ten lease years already elapsed, the Client faced a real trade-off: wait out the final year and risk losing the opportunity to a competing bidder or delay, or find a structure that gave them control now without breaching the letter of the allotment conditions.

## Our Approach: The Investment-as-Debt Model

We designed a phased structure that gives the Client operational and financial control immediately, while preserving the legal continuity the authority requires, and positions the Client for a clean, low-friction transfer to full ownership once the sale deed is executed.

- **Reconstitution, not replacement.** The three original allottees reconstitute themselves as an LLP and seek the authority’s approval for the change in constitution, a recognised, compliant route, rather than an attempted transfer of the allotment itself.

- **A capped equity position.** The Client (or a subsidiary) is inducted as a 49% partner. The original allottees retain 51%, satisfying the authority’s minimum-holding rule on paper in full.

- **Capital as senior debt, not equity.** Rather than infusing its investment as capital, the Client structures its funding as a secured loan or inter-corporate deposit to the entity. This does two things: it keeps the Client’s formal equity stake within the regulatory cap, and it gives the Client priority repayment rights over the entity’s revenue, ahead of any distribution to the 51% partners.

- **Control through a Development Management Agreement.** A DMA gives the Client sole managerial authority over construction, marketing, and site operations from day one. The original allottees are compensated through a fixed upfront payment or a modest revenue share, becoming passive financial beneficiaries rather than active operational partners.

- **A pre-agreed exit for the original allottees.** The agreement includes a binding buyout trigger: once the Absolute Sale Deed is executed, the 51% stake transfers to the Client automatically. Pre-signed transfer documentation, held subject to legal vetting, ensures this happens without renegotiation risk at the finish line.

## Where the Strategy Creates an Opening

Two elements of the current policy environment work in the Client’s favour and are built into the roadmap:

- **Incentive eligibility without new-entrant competition.** Under the current 2025-30 industrial policy, existing enterprises that increase capital expenditure by 25% remain eligible for the same subsidy benefits as new enterprises, without having to compete for a fresh allotment. Because the Client is stepping into an existing lessee entity rather than acquiring a new one, this path stays open.

- **A possible accelerated exit from the 51% rule.** The authority’s regulations allow for relaxation of the minority-holding penalty where a project shows “substantial implementation.” Separately, current policy allows units that have run production successfully for two years to qualify for clear title. Beginning construction immediately, under the entity’s name, keeps both of these accelerants live, potentially shortening the runway to full title well ahead of the original ten-year mark.

## Risk Profile

We were candid with the Client that this structure carries two real, monitored risks:

- **Temporary minority status.** For a window of roughly 12-24 months, the Client’s formal position is a 49% stake, meaning the loan structuring and DMA are doing the real work of protecting its interests, not the equity position itself.

- **Ongoing regulatory scrutiny.** The authority monitors the entity’s balance sheet and implementation progress throughout. Failure to demonstrate production within the required window reintroduces resumption risk, making the construction timeline as much a legal milestone as an operational one.

## Why This Structure

The alternative, waiting out the remaining lease term, or attempting a direct transfer that could read as a disguised third-party right, carried a much higher risk profile: potential resumption of the land without compensation, loss of subsidy eligibility, and a live risk of the opportunity being lost to a competing allottee altogether.

By keeping legal title exactly where the regulator expects it to sit, and using financial and contractual structuring, not equity, to secure control, this approach let the Client move from zero control to full operational authority immediately, while preserving bankability, subsidy eligibility, and a clean path to eventual ownership.

## The Value We Added

What could easily have become a stalled expansion, or an expensive, high-risk workaround, became a structured, compliant path to ownership. Our role was to translate a rigid regulatory framework into a workable commercial structure: giving the Client immediate operational control and priority on its capital, without triggering the very restrictions the framework was designed to enforce.

In doing so, we protected the Client from resumption risk, kept the project’s subsidy eligibility intact under the current incentive policy, and converted a nine-year waiting problem into a near-term path to full title, turning a regulatory obstacle into a genuine first-mover advantage on a scarce industrial asset.

Bring us the question, the challenge or the opportunity. We’ll bring the experience and perspective to help you move forward with clarity.

# India’s Startup Redefinition 2026: Are You Still a “Startup” Under the New Norms?
Source: https://www.varishpartners.com/indias-startup-redefinition-2026/

By Varun ShenoyManaging Partner · 21 September 2026 · 2 min read

The Government of India just fundamentally changed the game for entrepreneurs. On February 5, 2026, the Ministry of Commerce and the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) issued a landmark notification that significantly expands who qualifies for “Startup” status. If you are a founder or an investor, these changes aren’t just administrative; they are strategic.

Here is what you need to know to stay compliant and maximise your benefits:

- **The ₹200 Crore Club:** The annual turnover threshold for being recognised as a startup has been doubled from ₹100 crore to ₹200 crore. The age cap remains at 10 years from incorporation. This move is specifically designed to accommodate enterprises with longer development and commercialisation timelines.

- **Deep Tech Finally Gets Its Own Lane:** In a significant policy shift, the government has formally defined “Deep Tech” as a distinct category. These entities, focused on new scientific or engineering knowledge and high R&D expenditure, now enjoy an extended recognition window of 20 years (up from 10) and a massive turnover ceiling of ₹300 crore. This acknowledges the long gestation periods and high capital intensity required to move India from a nation of technology adoption to one of technology innovation.

- **Inclusive Innovation, Cooperatives Are In:** In a major stride for grassroots innovation, startup recognition has been extended to cooperative enterprises, including multi-state and state-registered societies. This is a massive opportunity for founders in agriculture, rural industries and community-based sectors.

- **The “No-Go” Zones (Safeguards against Misuse):** With wider eligibility comes tighter oversight. The government has built in safeguards to prevent the misuse of the startup tag.

- Entities formed by splitting or reconstructing an existing business do not qualify.

- Startups are strictly prohibited from investing in real estate, automobiles, jewellery, or speculative or non-productive assets.

- Lending activities are barred unless they are a substantial part of the core business model.

## Why this matters for your strategy

While these changes unlock a meaningful pool of capital and extend the life of many high-quality ventures, as per the official data, only about 2% of recognised startups currently receive the Section 80-IAC tax benefits. Scaling past the old ₹100 crore limit no longer means an automatic exit from policy support, but it does mean your compliance and R&D documentation must be more robust than ever.

Ensure your business model is ready to leverage these new thresholds and that your growth strategy aligns with these updated norms.

# MSME Reforms 2026: Why Faster Payments Matter
Source: https://www.varishpartners.com/msme-reforms-2026-why-faster-payments-matter/

By Varun ShenoyManaging Partner · 21 September 2026 · 2 min read

You can have strong orders and healthy margins, but if customers don’t pay on time, growth can quickly become a working capital crisis.

That is why the MSMED (Amendment) Bill, 2026, recently passed by Parliament, is significant.

The reforms focus strongly on one of the biggest challenges faced by MSMEs: delayed payments.

## What changes?

- **50% interim payment:** If a buyer challenges an award in court and the matter remains pending for more than six months, the court will be required to direct payment of at least 50% of the awarded amount, subject to the amended law.

- **Time-bound dispute resolution:** Mediation is proposed to be completed within 90 days, followed by defined timelines for arbitration.

- **Stronger recovery:** Mediated settlements and arbitration awards can be recovered as arrears of land revenue.

- **Greater use of TReDS:** Central Public Sector Enterprises will be required to use TReDS for settlement of MSME invoices, helping businesses access working capital against receivables.

- **More Facilitation Councils:** States will have greater flexibility to establish MSEFCs, potentially helping reduce the backlog of delayed payment disputes.

- **Decriminalisation:** Certain offences will move towards warnings and graded civil penalties rather than criminal consequences.

## Why does this matter?

For a small business, an unpaid ₹20 lakh or ₹50 lakh invoice isn’t just an accounting entry.

It can mean delayed salaries, supplier payments, tax payments, inventory purchases and expansion plans.

The real objective of these reforms is therefore bigger than simply recovering outstanding invoices.

It is about giving MSMEs greater certainty over their cash flows.

Of course, legislation is only the beginning. The real test will be implementation, faster dispute resolution, effective enforcement, wider TReDS adoption and greater awareness among MSMEs.

If implemented well, these reforms could make a meaningful difference to India’s small businesses.

For MSMEs, getting paid on time isn’t just about cash. It’s about having the confidence to grow.

# Mastering Cash Flow: Essential Strategies to Keep Your Business Thriving
Source: https://www.varishpartners.com/mastering-cash-flow-essential-strategies-to-keep-your-business-thriving/

###
Varun Shenoy

All Posts

Managing cash flow is one of the most critical aspects of running a successful business. Whether you’re a startup or an established business, maintaining a steady cash flow ensures that you have the necessary resources to keep your operations running smoothly, pay employees, and handle unexpected expenses. Here are key strategies for monitoring and optimizing your cash flow:

**1. Monitor Cash Regularly**

One of the most essential practices in financial management is to monitor available cash regularly. Keeping a close eye on your cash flow allows you to understand how long your business can continue to operate without additional funding—often referred to as your “runway time.”

Regular monitoring helps you spot issues early, such as overspending, cash shortages, or delayed payments. To do this effectively:

- Track expenses and inflows rigorously.

- Be aware of major transactions and movements in your accounts.

- Review financial reports frequently, either daily or weekly, depending on your business size.

- Proactive monitoring provides better control over your finances and helps you make informed decisions.

**2. Make Use of Payment Periods**

Suppliers and vendors often provide a grace period for payments. This period acts as a buffer, giving you additional time before a bill is due. To maximize your cash on hand, negotiate with your suppliers for the longest payment period possible and always pay towards the end of the agreed period.

Negotiating favourable terms with suppliers can significantly improve your cash flow, allowing you to keep more cash in your business for a longer period. Remember, negotiations are a key part of maintaining healthy business relationships, and suppliers often appreciate transparency and open communication.

**3. Incentivize Early Payments from Customers**

If you operate in a B2B environment, incentivizing your customers for early payments can be an effective cash flow strategy. Offer discounts or other rewards for customers who pay ahead of time. This approach not only improves your cash inflow but also encourages reliable payment behavior from your clients.

By implementing early payment incentives, you may be able to reduce the time you wait for payment, giving you quicker access to working capital.

**4. Seek External Funds for Major Purchases**

One common mistake businesses make is using their available cash to finance large purchases, such as equipment, real estate, or major inventory orders. Instead, consider seeking external funding for these expenditures through loans, lines of credit, or other financial instruments.

Maintaining cash within your business is crucial because cash shortages can lead to operational challenges or even failure. External funding spreads out the cost of major purchases over time, preserving your working capital for day-to-day operations.

**5. Consider Renting or Leasing Equipment**

When deciding between buying, renting, or leasing equipment, carefully weigh the cost-benefit of each option. In many cases, renting or leasing equipment may be the smarter financial move. It often proves to be cheaper upfront and can eliminate the burden of maintenance and repairs, as the responsibility for upkeep typically remains with the owner of the equipment.

However, in some situations, ownership might be more cost-effective in the long run. Before making any decisions, perform a detailed cost-benefit analysis to ensure you’re making the right financial choice for your business.

**6. Maintain Sufficient Cash Reserves**

Unexpected expenses and business challenges are inevitable, no matter how well you plan. For this reason, it’s crucial to maintain a healthy cash reserve. Having sufficient reserves enables you to handle unforeseen expenses without causing a cash crunch.

Whether it’s an economic downturn, a delayed customer payment, or a sudden operational expense, having reserve cash acts as a financial safety net. Properly managing reserves reduces the likelihood of severe cash flow problems and helps your business remain resilient in the face of adversity.

**Conclusion**

Cash flow issues are a reality for many businesses, but with proper planning, they can be avoided. Regularly monitoring your finances, utilizing favourable payment periods, incentivizing early payments, seeking external funding for large purchases, and maintaining a sufficient cash reserve are all critical strategies for keeping your business’s cash flow healthy. By taking these steps, you can avoid the pitfalls that many businesses face and ensure long-term success for your venture.

# Optimizing Pricing Strategy for a Wholesaler
Source: https://www.varishpartners.com/optimizing-pricing-strategy-for-a-wholesaler/

Case Study #1

## Optimizing Pricing Strategy for a Wholesaler

**Client Challenge** 

A wholesaler in the consumer goods sector approached Varish Partners with a significant challenge: one dominant retailer accounted for approximately 60% of their sales. Despite already being offered the lowest prices, the retailer demanded additional discounts to support a promotional campaign, requiring at least a 30% discount to execute the sale. The wholesaler was concerned about the financial impact of further price reductions and sought a solution to determine the lowest price they could afford while maintaining profitability. 

**Objective** 

The client needed a comprehensive cost analysis to identify how low they could go on pricing without undermining their profit margins. Varish Partners was tasked with creating a full cost calculation model that could account for fixed and variable costs and simulate potential pricing scenarios based on varying sales volumes. 

**Varish Partners’ Approach** 

- **Cost Structure Analysis** 
We began by working closely with the client to understand their cost structure. This involved categorizing costs into two main components: fixed costs (e.g., warehouse rent, staff salaries, equipment depreciation) and variable costs (e.g., cost of materials & packaging). A detailed breakdown was conducted to ensure that all relevant expenses were accounted for. 

- **Baseline Calculation** 
Using the client’s current sales volume, we calculated the total cost per unit 

- **Modeling Various Sales Scenarios** 
To explore the impact of the retailer’s proposed promotional campaign, we developed a model to simulate how the total cost per unit would change with increased sales volume. This model demonstrated how fixed costs per unit would decrease as sales volumes increased, allowing for greater pricing flexibility. 

- **Optimized Pricing Recommendations** 
With the new cost data, we were able to calculate the lowest price the client could offer while still covering their costs and ensuring a reasonable profit margin. This allowed us to determine the feasibility of the retailer’s requested 30% discount. 

**Outcome** 

By partnering with Varish Partners, the client gained valuable insights into their cost structure and was equipped with a clear strategy for setting pricing based on different sales volumes. Our detailed cost model empowered them to confidently offer the additional discounts requested by the retailer, knowing they could still achieve profitability if the campaign successfully boosted sales. 

As a result, the client was able to: 

- Secure the retailer’s promotional campaign, maintaining their dominant position in the retailer’s product range. 

- Offer competitive pricing without compromising margins, ensuring long-term profitability. 

- Strengthen their relationship with the retailer by supporting their marketing efforts with well-calculated discounts.
